subject.title: fix: treat trusted-proxy gateway auth as doctor auth proof

question: Should the doctor exposure check accept documented, bounded trusted-proxy CIDRs as authentication proof, or intentionally require exact proxy hosts despite the runtime CIDR contract?
rationale: The patch changes the severity of a security diagnostic. Current runtime and documentation support CIDRs, but the acceptable boundary for downgrading an exposed-gateway finding requires an explicit owner decision.

options.title: Align doctor with runtime CIDRs
options.body: Accept narrow, non-broad CIDRs that remain viable under the runtime source and local-interface guards, with regression coverage for warning and critical cases.

options.title: Keep exact-host-only proof
options.body: Retain the proposed stricter doctor policy, but document that CIDR-based trusted-proxy setups intentionally remain critical despite being runtime-valid.

recommendation.title: Align doctor with runtime CIDRs
recommendation.body: Accept narrow, non-broad CIDRs that remain viable under the runtime source and local-interface guards, with regression coverage for warning and critical cases.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the trusted-proxy runtime and configuration contract that the doctor classification must either follow or intentionally narrow.
